Table structure analysis:

- Row 2: Scale type: Multiple range scale | Multi-interval scale (colspan 2) | Multiple range scale | Multi-interval scale (colspan 2)
- Accuracy class: (IIII) colspan 3 | (III) colspan 3
- Design variant: Platform scale with long column | Platform scale compact | Platform scale with remote display on cable | (repeat for x1)
- Min (Min1|Min2): M799x0: 1 kg | 2 kg; M877x0 & M899x0: 1 kg (colspan 2); M799x1: 2 kg | 4 kg; M877x1 & M899x1: 2 kg
- Max (Max1|Max2): M799x0: 100 kg | 200 kg; M877x0 & M899x0: 100 kg | 200 kg; M799x1: 150 kg | 200 kg; M877x1 & M899x1: 150 kg | 200 kg
- e (e1|e2): all: 0.1 kg | 0.2 kg
- n (n1|n2): M799x0: 1000|1000; M877x0 & M899x0: 1000|1000; M799x1: 1500|1000; M877x1 & M899x1: 1500|1000
- Tare balancing range, subtractive: M799x0: (Max1|Max2); M877x0: ---; M899x0: Max2; M799x1: (Max1|Max2); M877x1: ---; M899x1: Max2
- Platform size: M799x0: 292 mm x 298 mm; M877x0 & M899x0: 289 mm x 280 mm; M799x1: 292 mm x 298 mm; M877x1 & M899x1: 289 mm x 280 mm
- Temperature range: all: 10 °C ... 40 °C

Footnote: "( ) Multi-interval or multiple range scale" — this explains the parentheses around accuracy class. I'll record as footnote.

Now, build JSON:

certificate:
- number: "R76/1992-DE1-08.02"
- scheme: "A"? Hmm — scheme A or B. OIML-CS scheme A is basic (certificate without AOS), scheme B with AOS. This is a traditional R76 certificate from 2008, before OIML-CS. The schema asks scheme (A|B). Traditional certificates... typically these are treated as scheme A (no AOS). Actually the OIML certificate system of 1992 had no scheme distinction; OIML-CS introduced scheme A (basic) and B (with AOS). Given this certificate is issued without AOS, scheme A seems most reasonable. But should I guess? The instruction says don't fabricate. But the schema field exists. Many extractors put scheme: "A" for these. I'll use "A" since there's no mention of AOS.
- project_number: not present → omit. Actually "R3-0033" appears — that might be an internal PTB number. Hmm, hard to say. Could be a form number. I'll omit.

  - minimum_capacity (min): varies per model? Min: M799x0: 1 kg, M877x0: 1 kg, M899x0: 1 kg, M799x1: 2 kg, M877x1: 2 kg, M899x1: 2 kg. But note Min1|Min2 — for multiple range scales there are two ranges: Min1/Min2, Max1/Max2, e1/e2, n1/n2. For multi-interval scales, Min is single but Max is Max1|Max2 (two intervals).

Hmm, how to represent? Options:
- Separate attributes: minimum_capacity_range_1, minimum_capacity_range_2, maximum_capacity_range_1, maximum_capacity_range_2, verification_scale_interval_e1, e2, n1, n2.

For multi-interval (colspan) cells: Min given as single value "1 kg" → applies Min (no subscript). Max: "100 kg | 200 kg" for M877x0/M899x0 — Max1|Max2 (multi-interval has Maxi with ei). e: "0.1 kg | 0.2 kg". n: "1000 | 1000".
